steps.note: S1.2.1 states that rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx) and rows 6-7 restore c,a, so the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c, as in the paper.
S1.2.2 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, says the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one cases (zero and two already vanish), and gives self coefficient one.
S1.2.3 gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side term for intersections zero and two, with intersection one contributing zero and self coefficient one.
S1.2.4 gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), and the S1.2 method has each invocation restore its scratch wires.

The plan names the orthogonal residual of each edge (S1.4.1 method) and says edges join comparable labels (S1.4.1.5), but it never gives the per-edge residuals and their dimensions (the residual table).
S1.4.1.4 has t_X perp t_Y giving <t_X> in t_Y^perp only as the label inclusion along the side wire (paper line 953); it never gives the residual of side edge 2->5, <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.
The plan has center 3->4 as the only decreasing edge, losing h; sources N and sinks Wm-N; gate-wise telescoping to the signed sum Wm-2N; and Ic edges of loss h, so L=Ich, adding 2L to give Wm-2N+2L.

S1.4.1.7b says every nonzero F_2 residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one coordinate unit, hence is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis, with alternating planes absorbed via w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S1.4.1.7c states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 exactly.

S1.4.1.9.2 derives weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors from the wt(z+w) identity, and S1.4.1.9 and S1.4.1.9.3 decompose the phase difference over an orthonormal basis of the residual, with coefficient wt(v) for each v.
S1.4.1.9.3 says wt(v) is odd, so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]} = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}, which H diag(1,-1) H = X turns into aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The plan states the multi-column form where the paper applies it: each residual direction h gives one factor (C^{eps_h})^{tensor f} acting on all f columns of a slot (S1.4.4.1.4), with s_c such factors over the network (S1.4.4.1.7).

S1.4.4.1.9 restates the proposition and mentions C=iZC^{-1}Z turning the 27 inverse factors on X_a->Y_a into forward ones, but omits the endpoint frames (I for the zero label, C^{tensor m} for the full label) that make telescoping give C^{tensor m}, and does not specify the Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} corrections, so the result is asserted rather than derived.
The plan has both loss ratios below 1/2, so the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0 give s<Wm for both networks.
S1.4.2.1 states eta_c = 73/19906842167500 exactly.
The plan says both deficits exceed 20*2^-50 and log m<20, so m^{1-2^-50} > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), giving s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

S1.4.3.1.2 takes the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row as pivot, clears by lower-triangular column and row operations, deletes that row and column and repeats; S1.4.3.1.1 gives Pi exactly a ones.

S1.4.3.1.3 chooses a prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators, so the triangular updates work over Z/q^b with diagonal units, the specialisation the paper makes (stated compactly, without the finite table).
S1.4.3.1.3 says a lower-triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order, each by a diagonal unit plus a fixed combination of earlier coordinates.
The plan realises each one (i,j) of Pi as D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j, giving (h+d,d) with one interchange each and a in all.
The plan gives E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu through B<=m^nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3}=20 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}); C_0 appears only through 128mB^2 d^{nu+3} <= C_0 d^{C_1}, and nu=11 is not stated.

S1.4.4.4.1 gives A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf, with E bounding the scalar gates (24W^3), the child corrections (4s) and the bank corrections; S1.4.4.4.2 explains the factor s rather than s/W.
The plan unrolls with sx+E<=Bx to A(e)<=8dB^{k+1}, uses B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu to get A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and bounds the total by 128mB^2 d^{nu+3}<=C_0 d^{C_1}.
The plan puts values at depth l in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l by induction, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact, and epsilon*C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p).
S1.4.4.5.3 says every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and componentwise truncation errs by less than sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: P05 states 23 of the 26 sub-steps. All four bank-exchange steps, all four rank-saving steps, all four matrix-shear steps and all five simultaneous-layer steps are present. Three are absent. In the label budget, the residual table (L1) and the side-edge residual <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2 (L2) are missing; the plan has only the label inclusion from t_X perp t_Y. In the phase interface, the endpoint-frame argument (P4) is missing: the plan asserts the telescoped C^{tensor m} and the C=iZC^{-1}Z repair without the I and C^{tensor m} endpoint frames or the explicit Z_{a,k} corrections.
